workflow:
# Working in Figma — own the brief, build in sections

You are the designer, not a typist waiting for the next instruction. A one-line brief ("a portfolio about page", "a pricing section with three plans") is enough to deliver a finished, polished design. The official Figma MCP works the same way: discover the system, build a section per call, look once per section, fix, finish.

## Initiative — what you decide without asking
- Structure: which sections, in what order, what each contains.
- Content: real-sounding headings, copy, numbers, names. When a fact belongs to the user (their bio, prices, clients), write a plausible placeholder and list it in your final message as "replace these" — never stop the build to ask.
- Visual language: reuse the file's styles, type and spacing; where it has none, choose a coherent palette and type pairing (figma_suggest_fonts) and apply it everywhere.
- Richness: icons (svg), images (image url), decorative shapes (polygon, star, vector paths, lines, boolean shapes), dividers, badges, shadows — a design of only rectangles and text looks like a wireframe.
- Components: anything that repeats (card, row, chip, button) becomes a component once; place instances.
Ask the user only when a choice would change the whole result and no sensible default exists (which of two files, a brand they have not shown you). Otherwise pick, build, and say what you picked.

## 1. Orient (once per task)
- figma_status — follow `build.restart` if present ("plugin": re-run the plugin; "client": restart the MCP client).
- figma_get_selection, figma_get_pages — the user's context and where you are.
- figma_get_design_context on an existing screen: spacing scale, type scale, radius, colours, structure, and `stylesUsed` (style ids — library styles included). figma_get_styles / figma_get_variable_defs / figma_get_local_components for local tokens and components.

## 2. Plan briefly, then place the wrapper
Name the sections and each one's auto-layout in a sentence or two (no need to show the user a plan unless they asked). Find an empty spot (figma_get_design_context with depth 1 on the page) and create the wrapper: figma_create_frame { name, x, y, width: 1440 (desktop) | 390 (mobile), layout: "vertical", background }.

## 3. Build one section per call
figma_create_from_spec { parentId: <wrapper>, spec } — a complete section: its frames, text, shapes, icons, images and instances, with auto-layout throughout. Topic "spec" has the grammar; topic "build" has a worked example. Each call is one undo step and returns every id with its path.

## 4. Look after each section — then fix
- figma_check_layout { nodeId: <section> } — fix every error and warning (overflow, overlap, covered text, clipping, contrast).
- figma_export_node { nodeId: <section> } — held to 1024 px on its longest side by default [C-092], because a long build sends many renders; raise maxSize only when a detail is too small to judge. Judge hierarchy, rhythm, alignment, colour, polish.
- Fix with targeted edits (figma_set_auto_layout, figma_resize_nodes, figma_set_text_properties, figma_set_fills, figma_move_nodes…) — never rebuild a section that is mostly right.

## 5. Finish
- figma_check_layout on the whole wrapper: ok: true.
- One final render of the whole design.
- figma_select + figma_zoom_to, then tell the user what you built, the choices you made, and the placeholder content to replace.

## When to go element by element
Small edits to an existing design, or fixing one thing: use the granular tools directly (figma_create_text, figma_set_text, figma_move_nodes, …). For anything new and larger than a few nodes, build by section.

# Building a design, section by section

Example — "a pricing section with three plans" in a file whose screens use 24 padding, 16 gap, radius 12, Inter:

1. figma_get_design_context on an existing screen → padding 24, gap 16, radius 12, Inter, brand #4f46e5, stylesUsed ids.
2. Wrapper: figma_create_frame { name: "Pricing", x: <empty spot>, y: 0, width: 1440, layout: "vertical", padding: "96,120,96,120", gap: 48, alignX: "center", background: "#ffffff" } → WRAP
3. Heading section, one call:
   figma_create_from_spec { parentId: WRAP, spec: {"type":"frame","name":"Heading","layout":"vertical","gap":12,"alignX":"center","sizing":{"width":"fill"},"children":[
     {"type":"text","name":"Eyebrow","content":"PRICING","fontSize":13,"weight":"Semi Bold","color":"#4f46e5","letterSpacing":1.5},
     {"type":"text","name":"Title","content":"Simple plans that grow with you","fontSize":44,"weight":"Bold","align":"center"},
     {"type":"text","name":"Subtitle","content":"Start free, upgrade when your team does.","fontSize":18,"color":"#6b7280","align":"center"}]} }
4. The card, ONCE, as a component: figma_create_from_spec { parentId: WRAP, spec: {"type":"component","name":"Plan card","layout":"vertical","width":360,"gap":16,"padding":32,"cornerRadius":16,"background":"#ffffff","stroke":"#e5e7eb","children":[
     {"type":"svg","name":"Plan icon","svg":"<svg ...>","width":28,"color":"#4f46e5"},
     {"type":"text","name":"Plan","content":"Pro","fontSize":15,"weight":"Semi Bold"},
     {"type":"text","name":"Price","content":"$29 / month","fontSize":40,"weight":"Bold"},
     {"type":"frame","name":"Features","layout":"vertical","gap":10,"sizing":{"width":"fill"},"children":[ {"type":"text","content":"Unlimited projects","fontSize":15} ]},
     {"type":"button","name":"CTA","sizing":{"width":"fill"},"background":"#4f46e5","cornerRadius":10,"alignX":"center","children":[{"type":"text","content":"Start free trial","color":"#ffffff","weight":"Semi Bold"}]}]} } → CARD
   Then figma_add_component_property { componentId: CARD, name: "Plan", type: "TEXT", defaultValue: "Pro", bindNodeIds: [<Plan text id>] } (and Price) so instances change copy without detaching.
5. The row of plans, one call — each instance sets its own properties in the spec: figma_create_from_spec { parentId: WRAP, spec: {"type":"frame","name":"Plans","layout":"horizontal","gap":24,"children":[{"type":"instance","componentId":CARD},{"type":"instance","componentId":CARD,"properties":{"Plan":"Team","Price":"$79 / month"}},{"type":"instance","componentId":CARD,"properties":{"Plan":"Enterprise","Price":"Custom"}}]} }. figma_set_instance_properties changes one later.
6. Look: figma_check_layout { nodeId: WRAP } → fix; figma_export_node { nodeId: WRAP } → judge.
7. Polish: highlight the middle plan (figma_set_strokes, figma_set_effects for a shadow, a "Most popular" badge via figma_create_from_spec with a star or pill), apply the file's styles (figma_apply_style_to_node), and emphasis inside text with figma_set_text_range.
8. Finish: check_layout ok:true, figma_select + figma_zoom_to, report choices and placeholders.

## Auto-layout, the way designers use it
- Structure is nested auto-layout: page (column) → sections (column, fill width) → rows (row) → items. Absolute x/y only for deliberate overlap (decoration, badges): inside a frame with layout "none", or as one child of an auto-layout frame that leaves the flow — "positioning": "absolute" in the spec, or figma_move_nodes { nodeIds, positioning: "absolute", x, y } on an existing layer.
- Spacing from gap and padding on one scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96) — never from nudging.
- Sizing per axis: a number = fixed, "hug" fits content, "fill" takes the parent's space. Text in a column fills and wraps; a paragraph in a row needs a width.
- Hierarchy: one clear size per level (body 15–18, headings 28–64, display up to 120+), line height ~1.5× body and ~1.1–1.2× headings, at most two families and three weights.
- Contrast: body text at least 4.5:1, large text 3:1.

## Making it look designed, not generated
- Give each section one focal point (a big number, an image, a bold heading) and quieter support.
- Use shape for character: a soft vector blob behind a hero image, a polygon or star badge, thin lines as dividers or connectors, a boolean cut-out, a dotted grid (figma_set_layout_grids is for the editor only — draw a pattern with shapes if it should be visible).
- Real icons (svg) and images (image url) instead of grey boxes; crop photos with cornerRadius and scaleMode "fill".
- Consistent radius and stroke weight across the design; shadows soft and few.
design-system:
# Using (and creating) the file's design system

Read:
- figma_get_styles — paint, text, effect and grid styles, each with its value, key and bound variables.
- figma_get_variable_defs — collections and modes, and every variable's value per mode, scopes and codeSyntax. With { nodeId }, only the tokens that screen uses, resolved.
- figma_get_local_components — components and variant sets; figma_get_component for one's properties, variants and key.
- Styles from a team library are NOT in figma_get_styles (it lists local styles). Read them off an existing screen: figma_get_design_context returns `stylesUsed` with each style's `id` and `key` (remote: true for library styles) — apply those ids with figma_apply_style_to_node { styleId }.
- Library variables: figma_get_library_variables lists them by collection; figma_import_library_assets { assets: [{ kind, key }] } brings a library component, set, style or variable into the file by key. Keys come from figma_get_design_context (`componentsUsed`, `stylesUsed`, `variablesUsed`) on a screen that uses them, or from the library file opened in a second session.

Apply instead of raw values:
- figma_apply_style_to_node { nodeIds, styleName, type? } — a paint style on fill (default) or stroke, a text style, an effect style.
- **A text style is not only a font — it is font, size, line height, letter spacing and case.** Applying one to a node of a different rank does not restyle it, it replaces its type: measured on a real screen, applying a 15 px label style took a 200 px display heading down to Silkscreen 15. Match a text style to nodes of the same kind (a label style on labels, a body style on body), and leave display type on raw values — the pages of a file usually do exactly that. Read the pairing off an existing screen before applying anything: figma_get_design_context reports each node's `styles.text`, and nodes of the same rank share one.
- figma_bind_variable_to_node { nodeIds, field, variableName } — field: fill, stroke, radius, gap, padding, width, height, opacity, or any Figma bindable field.
- figma_create_instance { componentId } — never redraw a component that exists. Change an instance's variant with figma_set_instance_properties ({"Size":"Large"}); figma_swap_component swaps it to a different component, and given a component SET it lands on the set's default variant.

Create a system when the file has none and the user wants one (topic "library" has the full playbook):
- tokens: figma_create_variable_collection, then a whole family per call with figma_create_variables (value strings: "#1a2b3c", "16", "true", "alias:color/blue/500"); scopes and codeSyntax later with figma_set_variable_properties.
- styles: figma_create_paint_style, figma_create_text_style, figma_create_effect_style.
- components: build the element (a spec with type "component", or an existing frame + figma_convert_to_component), then make it configurable with figma_add_component_property (TEXT for labels, BOOLEAN to show/hide an icon, INSTANCE_SWAP for a nested icon). Variants: name each component "Size=Large, State=Default", then figma_combine_as_variants. Instances change through figma_set_instance_properties — never detach to edit a label.
- light/dark: figma_add_variable_mode + figma_set_variable_value per mode (extra modes need a paid Figma plan — Figma's refusal is returned as is). A mode shows nowhere until a frame uses it: figma_set_variable_mode { nodeIds: [<frame>], collectionName, mode: "Dark" }.

figma_check_layout lists raw colours when the file has styles or variables they should be bound to; { audit: ["tokens"] } names each unbound colour, spacing and radius.
typography:
# Typography — choosing fonts that fit, and applying them

1. figma_suggest_fonts { mood, use, nodeId? }
   - mood: the feel in words ("modern minimal", "editorial elegant", "playful", "technical", "luxury", "friendly").
   - use: ui | mobile | marketing | editorial | code | brand.
   It reads the fonts the design already uses and the fonts THIS Figma can load, and returns ranked heading/body
   pairings with the exact style names, a type scale, and `applyPlan` (the existing text split into heading and body ids).
2. If the design already has a font (`consistency`), keep it unless the user asked for a change. Changing type is a
   whole-design decision: do it everywhere at once.
3. Apply a choice to existing text:
   figma_set_text_properties { nodeIds: applyPlan.headingNodeIds, fontFamily: <heading>, weight: <heading style> }
   figma_set_text_properties { nodeIds: applyPlan.bodyNodeIds, fontFamily: <body> }
   A new family keeps each run's own weight (bold words stay bold). Check `fellBack` in the result.
4. For new text, pass fontFamily / weight / fontSize / lineHeight from the scale to figma_create_text — or create text
   styles once (figma_create_text_style) and apply them with figma_apply_style_to_node, so the system stays consistent.
5. Emphasis inside a text: figma_set_text_range { nodeId, match: "Pro", weight: "Bold", color: … } — never split one
   sentence into several text nodes to bold a word.

Rules that keep type looking designed:
- At most two families (one is often enough); hierarchy comes from size and weight first.
- Body 14–18 px with line height about 1.4–1.6×; headings tighter (1.1–1.3×), optionally -1% to -2% letter spacing.
- Few sizes, from one scale; at most two or three weights per screen.
- A display face (condensed, script, very bold) only at large sizes, never for paragraphs.
- Check contrast: figma_check_layout reports text below 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text).
design-to-code:
# From a Figma design to code

The render is the target and the data is the source: read both before writing a line, reuse what the project already has, and verify only what you were asked to build.

## Context
1. Target: the node the user names — a Figma link or an id like "12-34" goes in as `nodeId` unchanged — or figma_get_selection.
2. figma_get_design_context { nodeId } — sizes, auto-layout, constraints, text (with its styled runs), fills, effects, and the styles, variables and components each node uses, by name. `stylesUsed` carries each style's id, key and `remote` (true for a library style), not its value. figma_get_variable_defs { nodeId } gives the values of every style and variable this screen uses, library ones included, resolved; figma_get_styles lists only this file's local styles, so a library style is never there [C-081]. Follow `nextCursor` until `truncated` is false. On a large screen read `depth: 1` first, then each section by its id.
3. figma_export_node { nodeId } straight after — the visual target. It is NEVER an asset: do not ship it, and do not crop pieces out of it.
4. figma_get_reactions for what clicks and hovers do; figma_get_annotations for the designer's notes; figma_get_motion_context { nodeId } for animated layers — it reads every layer inside, because a screen never animates itself, only its layers do [C-115]. Design context marks each animated node with `motion`.
5. Text longer than 400 characters is cut in design context: raise `maxTextChars`, or read it whole with figma_scan_text_nodes.

## Implementation
- Inspect the project first: its component folders, token files and installed design-library packages. Reuse what matches; match instances to existing components by component name, variant set and properties.
- Map, do not transcribe: auto-layout column/row + gap + padding → flex or grid; alignMain/alignCross → justify/align; sizing fixed / hug / fill → fixed size / content size / flex: 1 or width: 100%; absolute positions only where the design really overlaps things.
- Tokens: style and variable names (and `codeSyntax` where set) → the project's tokens. When the two disagree, prefer the project's token and adjust minimally; mention the difference.
- Assets: figma_download_assets { nodeIds } for every image and icon — renders per the node's export settings, plus each image's original bytes without the layers drawn over it. Place every visible asset exactly in its slot; SVG icons keep their root width and height. Add no icon package, redraw nothing, and never ship a temporary URL.
- Motion (figma_get_motion_context): keyframes → CSS @keyframes or motion.dev; easing HOLD → steps(1, jump-end), "cubic:x1,y1,x2,y2" → cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2), "spring:<bounce>" → a motion.dev spring with that bounce; translation and rotation add up, scale multiplies; honour prefers-reduced-motion.
- Prototype reactions → the project's router, links and state; prototype transitions are not motion keyframes.
- Text: `openType` TNUM → font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, LIGA/CALT → font-feature-settings. SF Symbols come back as code points (`sfSymbols`): ask the user for the symbol name rather than guess.

## Verification
- Render your code at the export's size and compare it with figma_export_node.
- Verify only the requested scope; list other mismatches you noticed instead of fixing them unasked.
- Check each asset: the file exists and is not empty, it is used at its callsite, and it renders at the design's size.
check:
# Checking your own work

figma_check_layout { nodeId } — run it after every section and before you call anything done.
- text_overflow (error): a text that hugs its content ran past its parent. Make it fill the column (figma_resize_nodes { sizing: { horizontal: "fill" } }) or give it a width.
- overlap (error): two texts on top of each other. Fix the structure (auto-layout, gap), do not nudge.
- covered (error): a filled layer painted above a text hides part of it (the detail says how much). Move one of them or reorder (figma_reorder_nodes).
- clipped (error for text): part of a node is cut off by a parent that clips content. Make room, or when the clipping itself is the mistake: figma_set_clips_content { nodeIds: [<parent>], clipsContent: false }.
- text_collapsed (error): a text squeezed to a sliver, a word or less per line. Give it the column (sizing fill) or a width.
- outside_parent (warning): sticks out of its parent.
- fill_in_hug (warning): a child set to fill inside a parent that hugs on that axis — it collapses. Give the parent a size, or the child a fixed or hug size.
- low_contrast (warning): text below 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text) against what is behind it.
- zero_size (warning); empty_text, empty_frame, default_name (info) — name layers, remove leftovers.
- placeholder_text (info): "Title", "Button", "Lorem ipsum" left in — write the real copy.
- sibling_overlap (info): frames stacked on each other outside auto-layout — deliberate (a badge, a collage) or a layout bug.
- rawColors: raw hex where the file has styles or variables to use instead.
`ok: true` means no errors and no warnings.

Audits, on request: figma_check_layout { nodeId, audit: ["tokens", "names", "fonts"], expectFonts: ["Inter"] }
- tokens: unbound_color (warning), unbound_spacing / unbound_radius (info) — raw values where the file has tokens; `suggest` names the variable to bind.
- names: duplicate_name (warning) — two components with one name on a page, or two variants with one name in a set.
- fonts: wrong_font (warning) for free text outside expectFonts, ds_font_gap (info) inside instances or text styles; without expectFonts, `fonts` counts text per family.

After a library or a code-to-design build, run all three.

figma_export_node — the render, for judgement: spacing rhythm, alignment, hierarchy, colour, polish. A vision reading of a render has disagreed with the document about where things were, so take positions and sizes from figma_get_design_context or figma_get_node, not from the picture.
safety:
# Rules that keep you from destroying work

- Build at an empty spot. Before placing a new top-level frame, read where the existing ones are.
- Delete only ids that your own calls returned in this session (figma_delete_nodes). Never delete by name search, and never delete a frame you did not create without asking the user.
- figma_undo_step takes back the most recent tool call — and possibly a manual edit the user made since. Prefer figma_delete_nodes with your ids.
- Every write accepts idempotencyKey. After a timeout, retry with the SAME key: it never runs twice.
- A failure carries partial.created (what exists) and partial.failedAt (where it stopped): continue from there, or delete those ids.
- Every error says `safeToRetry`. true: nothing changed, fix the input and call again. false: something may have changed — read the nodes (figma_get_node / figma_get_nodes_info) before you retry, or you build it twice.
- figma_status: `build.restart: "plugin"` → the plugin is an older build, ask the user to close and re-run it; `"client"` → this server is older than the build on disk, ask the user to restart the MCP client (re-running the plugin changes nothing). No `restart` → never ask for one.
- Tell the user what you changed, with node names, when you finish.
tools:
# Choosing a tool

| Intent | Tool |
|---|---|
| Is Figma connected, is everything current | figma_status (follow build.restart) |
| What the user selected | figma_get_selection |
| Pages | figma_get_pages, figma_navigate_page, figma_create_page |
| Understand a design | figma_get_design_context (follow nextCursor) |
| One node / several nodes | figma_get_node, figma_get_nodes_info |
| Find things | figma_search_nodes, figma_scan_nodes_by_types, figma_scan_text_nodes |
| The design system | figma_get_design_context (stylesUsed, incl. library), figma_get_styles (local, with values), figma_get_variable_defs (values per mode; { nodeId } for one screen's tokens), figma_get_local_components, figma_get_component, figma_get_fonts |
| Team libraries | figma_get_library_variables, figma_import_library_assets (components, sets, styles, variables by key) |
| **A whole section or screen** | **figma_create_from_spec** (frames, text, shapes, svg icons, images, instances in one call) |
| A single container | figma_create_frame (+ figma_set_auto_layout to change it later) |
| Text | figma_create_text, figma_set_text, figma_find_replace_text |
| Typography | figma_suggest_fonts, figma_set_text_properties, figma_set_text_range |
| Icons and images | figma_import_svg, figma_import_image |
| Shapes | figma_create_rectangle, figma_create_ellipse, figma_create_polygon, figma_create_star, figma_create_line, figma_create_vector (any SVG path) |
| Shape operations | figma_boolean_nodes (union / subtract / intersect / exclude), figma_flatten_nodes, figma_set_mask |
| Components | figma_convert_to_component, figma_combine_as_variants, figma_add_component_property, figma_edit_component_property, figma_delete_component_property, figma_create_instance, figma_set_instance_properties, figma_swap_component, figma_detach_instance |
| Slots | figma_create_slot, figma_reset_slot |
| Descriptions and doc links | figma_set_description (components, sets, styles, variables) |
| Paint | figma_set_fills, figma_set_strokes, figma_set_corner_radius, figma_set_effects, figma_set_opacity, figma_set_blend_mode |
| Clip content | figma_set_clips_content |
| Layout grids | figma_set_layout_grids, figma_create_grid_style |
| Tokens | figma_create_variables (a family per call), figma_set_variable_properties (scopes, codeSyntax), figma_update_variable_collection, figma_apply_style_to_node, figma_bind_variable_to_node, figma_create_variable…, figma_create_…_style, figma_update_style |
| Show a mode (e.g. Dark) | figma_set_variable_mode |
| Arrange | figma_move_nodes, figma_resize_nodes (width, height, sizing), figma_rotate_nodes, figma_reorder_nodes, figma_reparent_nodes, figma_group_nodes, figma_set_constraints |
| Duplicate | figma_clone_node (lands right after its source) |
| **A polish pass** (many small edits, one undo) | figma_batch |
| Check | figma_check_layout (audit for tokens, names, fonts), figma_export_node |
| Assets for code | figma_download_assets (renders + original image bytes) |
| Show the user | figma_select, figma_zoom_to |
| Remove your own work | figma_delete_nodes (ids you created) |
| Prototype | figma_set_reactions, figma_get_reactions, figma_set_scroll_behavior, figma_set_prototype_flows |
| Motion (timeline animation) | figma_get_motion_context, figma_set_keyframes, figma_remove_keyframes, figma_export_video (see it move) |

On a FigJam board (topic figjam):

| Intent | Tool |
|---|---|
| Read the board | figma_get_design_context (stickies, shapes, connectors with their `connectors` edge list, tables, code), figma_get_metadata (`board`: top-level sections, counts by type) |
| **A zone** (section, title, stickies or cards, connectors by ref) | **figma_create_from_spec** with the FigJam types |
| Many stickies into an existing zone | figma_create_stickies |
| Flowchart steps, decisions, databases | figma_create_shapes_with_text |
| Lines between nodes | figma_create_connectors (after the nodes exist; never move them later), figma_edit_connectors |
| Rows and columns of data | figma_create_table, figma_edit_table (cells, rows, columns) |
| Code, a web page | figma_create_code_block, figma_create_link_preview |
| Colour by palette name, wide stickies, shape type, code language | figma_set_board_properties |
| Fit sections to their content | figma_fit_sections |
| Check a zone | figma_check_layout (audit board) |

In a Figma Slides deck (topic slides):

| Intent | Tool |
|---|---|
| The deck: rows, slides, notes | figma_get_slide_grid — start here |
| Add slides | figma_create_slides (3–5 per call), then figma_create_from_spec per slide |
| Reorder, regroup | figma_move_slides (a few slides), figma_set_slide_grid (the whole deck) |
| Skip a slide, speaker notes | figma_set_slide_properties |
| Transitions | figma_set_slide_transition |
| Check a batch of slides | figma_check_layout (nodeIds) |
| Focus a slide, grid or single view | figma_zoom_to (view) |
| The deck as one PDF | figma_export_frames_to_pdf (deck: true) |
spec:
# figma_create_from_spec — the spec grammar

The way to build anything new that is larger than a few nodes: one call per section (a header, a hero, a card, a grid of cards, a footer), placed into a wrapper frame by `parentId`. Each call is one undo step, and `created[]` returns every id with its path in the spec.

Node fields (all optional except as noted):
  type        "frame" | "text" | "button" | "rectangle" | "ellipse" | "polygon" | "star" | "line" | "vector"
              | "svg" | "image" | "component" | "instance" | "section"   (default "frame")
              On a FigJam board also "sticky" | "shape" | "table" | "code" | "connector" (see below).
              Only frame, button, component and section take children.
  name        layer name — name every layer for what it is; a section takes "" (no label)
  ref         a name for this node, unique in the call (letters, digits, _ and -). A connector names it as an end,
              and the result's `refs` maps every ref to its id.
  width, height, x, y      (x/y only inside a frame without auto-layout: deliberate overlap, decoration)
  layout      "vertical" | "horizontal" | "none"   (auto-layout)
  sizing      "fixed" | "hug" | "fill", or { "width": ..., "height": ... } per axis. An axis with a number is
              fixed; an auto-layout axis without one hugs, so { "height": 28 } is a fixed-height row that grows
              sideways. "fill" on a child takes the parent's space: along the parent's layout it absorbs the
              leftover room, across it it stretches. hug: auto-layout frames and text; fill: children of an
              auto-layout — anything else is refused.
  positioning "absolute" — a child that leaves its auto-layout parent's flow (a badge, a floating button); x/y place it
  gap, padding   padding: number or [top, right, bottom, left]
  wrap        true: a horizontal layout wraps into rows; rowGap (default: gap) between the rows,
              alignContent "auto" | "space-between" for the rows
  alignX, alignY  "start" | "center" | "end" | "space-between" (screen directions; space-between only along the layout);
              alignY "baseline" lines up the text baselines of a row
  background  hex colour, e.g. "#ffffff"; without it a nested frame is transparent, a frame on the page white
  fill        same as background (shapes)
  cornerRadius, stroke, strokeWeight, opacity, visible, locked, rotation (degrees)
  clipsContent   default false, so shadows are not cut off at the frame edge
  content     text content (type "text")
  fontFamily, fontSize, weight (number or style name), color, align (left | center | right | justified), lineHeight, letterSpacing
  pointCount  polygon sides / star spikes (>= 3);  innerRadius  star, 0–1
  path        type "vector": SVG path data, e.g. "M0 40 C60 0 120 80 180 40 L180 80 L0 80 Z"
  svg         type "svg": SVG markup (an icon); width or height scales it, color recolours it, or colorVariable
              binds it to a COLOR variable (name or id; not together with color)
  url         type "image": http(s) PNG/JPEG/GIF, fetched before anything is built; scaleMode fill | fit | crop | tile
  width + cap type "line": width is the length, rotation turns it; stroke/color, strokeWeight;
              cap none | round | square | arrow | arrow-filled | triangle | circle | diamond
  componentId type "instance" (no children): a COMPONENT or COMPONENT_SET id — or componentKey / componentSetKey
              for a library component, with variant "Size=Large, State=Hover" to pick one of a set
  properties  instance: { "Label": "Buy now", "Show icon": false } — set in the same call
  nested      instance: { "<nested instance layer name>": { "Label": "…" } } for instances inside it
  variableModes  frame / button / component / section: { "<collection name>": "<mode name>" }, e.g. { "Theme": "Dark" }
  variables   bind by variable name or id, e.g. { "fill": "color/bg", "radius": "radius/md", "gap": "space/4" }
              (an svg binds its colour with colorVariable, not variables.fill)
  style       apply a local style by name or id: { "fill" | "stroke" | "text" | "effect" | "grid": "Style name" }
              (a library style: apply it afterwards by id with figma_apply_style_to_node)
  children    array of the same shape, nested (a "component" is converted after its children are built)
  list        text: "unordered" | "ordered" | "none" — every line of the content becomes a bullet or a number. A
              list is ONE text with lines separated by \n, never a dot shape beside each line.

Sections (Design and FigJam) have no auto-layout. Instead:
  arrange     "row" | "column" | "grid:N" — places the children from their real sizes (a sticky grows with its
              text), rows as tall as their tallest item; a child of an arranged section takes no x/y
  gap         space between arranged children (default 64); padding  inset for arrange and hug (default 32)
  hug         true — the section fits its children plus padding, inner sections first; not with width/height
  contentsHidden   true hides what the section holds
  background  a hex (FigJam's section swatch names are not confirmed yet)

On a FigJam board, five more types (none takes children):
  sticky      content, color (white, gray, green, teal, blue, violet, pink, red, orange, yellow, or a hex), wide
              (416 wide instead of 240; a sticky has no width or height), authorVisible, x, y
  shape       shape (rounded-rectangle, square, ellipse, diamond, triangle-up, parallelogram-right, eng-database,
              eng-queue, eng-file, hexagon, chevron, speech-bubble, …, or "label" for a 1–2 character marker),
              content, color (a preset that sets fill, stroke and text: light-blue, green, gray, …) or fill /
              stroke / textColor as hex, width + height (default: fitted to the text), fontSize, x, y
  table       rows (an array of rows of strings; row 0 is the header) or numRows + numColumns, header,
              headerColor, fill, columnWidths, rowHeights, fontFamily, weight, fontSize, x, y
  code        content, language (typescript, javascript, python, sql, json, bash, …, plaintext), x, y
  connector   from, to — "<ref>", "<ref>@right" (magnets top, bottom, left, right, center), a node id, or "x,y";
              label, lineType (elbowed | straight | curved), startCap, endCap (none, arrow-lines, triangle-filled,
              erd-one-or-more, …), color, strokeWeight, dash ("dashed", "dotted", "10,6"), labelBackground.
              Built after every other node of the call, in the container that declares it, and never moved:
              it takes no x, y, width or height.

A whole board zone in one call — a section with a title, a grid of stickies, and a decision flow:
  figma_create_from_spec { parentId: <the board's wrapper section>, spec }
  {"type":"section","name":"","background":"#F5FBFF","arrange":"column","gap":40,"padding":[68,60,100,80],"hug":true,"children":[{"type":"text","content":"What went well","fontSize":48,"weight":"Bold"},{"type":"section","name":"","background":"#FFFFFF","arrange":"grid:3","hug":true,"children":[{"type":"sticky","content":"Shipped the beta on time","color":"green"},{"type":"sticky","content":"Pairing on the hard bugs","color":"green"},{"type":"sticky","content":"Reviews done within a day","color":"green"}]},{"type":"section","name":"","background":"#FFFFFF","arrange":"row","gap":120,"hug":true,"children":[{"type":"shape","ref":"idea","shape":"rounded-rectangle","content":"Keep pairing?","color":"light-blue"},{"type":"shape","ref":"vote","shape":"diamond","content":"Team agrees","color":"light-yellow"},{"type":"shape","ref":"plan","shape":"rounded-rectangle","content":"Pair every Tuesday","color":"light-green"},{"type":"connector","from":"idea@right","to":"vote@left"},{"type":"connector","from":"vote@right","to":"plan@left","label":"yes"}]}]}

Several roots: `spec` may be a JSON ARRAY of 1–50 roots when parentId or pageId says where they go — the whole
content of one slide, or the cards of one zone. Still one validation and one undo step; the result adds `rootIds`.

Editors:
  - A type the file's editor cannot build is refused before the first node, UNSUPPORTED with `failedAt` naming
    it: a component on a board, a sticky in a Design file, or a type whose create function the file's editor
    does not offer.
  - On a board, text defaults to Inter Medium in Charcoal #1E1E1E; in Design, Inter Regular in black.
  - On a slide, every node goes into its parent before its x/y is set, and the result's `drift` lists any
    position Figma moved. Expect []; never add an offset back by hand.

Notes that matter:
  - Fonts fall back Inter → Roboto → Arial → Helvetica Neue. A text entry in `created[]` carries `font` with
    `fellBack: true` when the font used is not the one asked for — never a silent substitution.
  - Types, layout, alignment, padding, colours, paths, image URLs and the variables/style maps are checked before
    anything is built; such a failure creates nothing.
  - A field the node type does not take is refused, with the nearest valid name — never silently ignored.
  - A mid-way failure does NOT roll back. You get `created[]`, the path in the spec that failed, and the ids built
    so far, so the user can press Ctrl+Z once (the whole call is one undo step) or you can continue from there.
  - Supply your own idempotencyKey for a large spec.

# Building a design library — tokens, styles, components

Order matters: variables before styles, styles before components, and every component bound to tokens. Names are deterministic, so a rerun finds what exists and continues; never delete to start over.

## 0. Read what exists — always first
- figma_get_variable_defs: collections, modes, values, scopes, codeSyntax. Copy the file's naming ("color/bg/default" or "Colors/Background"), its scope habits and its mode names; never start a second scheme.
- figma_get_styles and figma_get_local_components: what is there, with values, keys and variant properties.
- Team libraries: figma_get_library_variables lists their variables by collection key; figma_import_library_assets { assets: [{ kind, key }] } imports a component, set, style or variable. Keys come from figma_get_design_context (componentsUsed, stylesUsed, variablesUsed) on a screen that uses them, or from the library file opened in a second session.
Exit: you can name each existing token family and its naming pattern.

## 1. Foundations — primitives, then semantic aliases
- Primitives (the raw palette, the spacing scale, radii) in their own collection with `scopes: []`, so they never appear in Figma's pickers.
- Semantic tokens in a collection with modes (Light, Dark), each value an alias: "alias:color/blue/500". One figma_create_variables call per family, a value per mode; `ifExists: "skip"` resumes a half-built family.
- Scopes by role: backgrounds FRAME_FILL / SHAPE_FILL, text colour TEXT_FILL, borders STROKE_COLOR, spacing GAP, radii CORNER_RADIUS, sizes WIDTH_HEIGHT, type FONT_SIZE / LINE_HEIGHT / LETTER_SPACING.
- codeSyntax WEB as the codebase writes it: "var(--color-bg-default)". Change scopes, codeSyntax or names later with figma_set_variable_properties; rename collections and modes with figma_update_variable_collection.
- A mode shows on a frame only once applied: figma_set_variable_mode { nodeIds, collectionName, mode: "Dark" }.
Exit: figma_get_variable_defs lists every token with a value per mode, scopes and codeSyntax.

## 2. Styles
- The type ramp as text styles (figma_create_text_style), elevation as effect styles, layout grids as grid styles (figma_create_grid_style), paint styles bound to a variable (variableName).
- Change a style in place with figma_update_style: deleting and recreating it detaches every layer that uses it.
- figma_set_description on each: when to use it.
Exit: figma_get_styles shows each style's value and bound variables.

## 3. Components — one page each
- A page per component (figma_create_page), built with figma_create_from_spec, every fill, stroke, padding, gap and radius bound through `variables` — no raw values.
- Variants: name each component "Size=Large, State=Hover", build them all in ONE figma_create_from_spec, then figma_combine_as_variants { componentIds, columns: "State" } lays the set out as a grid. Keep a set at 30 combinations or fewer; split by a property beyond that.
- Properties: TEXT for labels, BOOLEAN to show or hide a part, INSTANCE_SWAP for icons with `preferredValues` (the icon components). Rename or rewire with figma_edit_component_property instead of deleting and re-adding.
- figma_set_description, with a documentationLink, on every set.
Exit per component: figma_check_layout { nodeId, audit: ["tokens", "names"] } reports no unbound_color, and figma_get_component shows the properties you meant.

## 4. Document and validate
- A foundations page: swatches filled from the semantic tokens, the type ramp as text in its styles.
- figma_check_layout { audit: ["tokens", "names", "fonts"] } on every page; fix each warning.
- Report what you built, by page, and anything you could not bind.

# Prototypes — interactions, scrolling and flows

Three places: interactions on layers (figma_set_reactions), scrolling and fixed layers on frames (figma_set_scroll_behavior), and the page's flows (figma_set_prototype_flows). Read the current state first with figma_get_reactions.

## Interactions — figma_set_reactions { nodeId, reactions }
`reactions` is a JSON array that replaces the node's list ([] removes them). Figma's full Reaction shape is accepted as is — copy one from figma_get_reactions — plus a shorthand for navigation. Use ids, never names: destinations from figma_get_node or design context, variables and modes from figma_get_variable_defs. Units differ: a transition's `duration` is seconds [C-056], a trigger's `timeout` (AFTER_TIMEOUT) and `delay` (MOUSE_ENTER, MOUSE_LEAVE, MOUSE_UP, MOUSE_DOWN) are milliseconds [C-122] — 0.3 and 2000, never 300 and 2.

Navigate on click with smart animate (shorthand):
  [{"trigger":"ON_CLICK","action":{"type":"NODE","destinationId":"12:3","transition":"SMART_ANIMATE","duration":0.3,"easing":"EASE_OUT"}}]
Open an overlay:
  [{"trigger":"ON_CLICK","action":{"type":"NODE","destinationId":"12:40","navigation":"OVERLAY","transition":"DISSOLVE","duration":0.2}}]
After a delay of 2 s:
  [{"trigger":{"type":"AFTER_TIMEOUT","timeout":2000},"actions":[{"type":"NODE","destinationId":"12:3","navigation":"NAVIGATE","transition":null}]}]
On a key (Enter is 13):
  [{"trigger":{"type":"ON_KEY_DOWN","device":"KEYBOARD","keyCodes":[13]},"actions":[{"type":"BACK"}]}]
Set a variable — variableValue is Figma's VariableData:
  [{"trigger":"ON_CLICK","actions":[{"type":"SET_VARIABLE","variableId":"VariableID:1:2","variableValue":{"type":"BOOLEAN","resolvedType":"BOOLEAN","value":true}}]}]
Switch a mode (light to dark):
  [{"trigger":"ON_CLICK","actions":[{"type":"SET_VARIABLE_MODE","variableCollectionId":"VariableCollectionId:1:1","variableModeId":"1:2"}]}]
Branch on a boolean variable — the block without a condition is the else; actions inside a block use the full shape:
  [{"trigger":"ON_CLICK","actions":[{"type":"CONDITIONAL","conditionalBlocks":[
    {"condition":{"type":"VARIABLE_ALIAS","resolvedType":"BOOLEAN","value":{"type":"VARIABLE_ALIAS","id":"VariableID:1:2"}},
     "actions":[{"type":"NODE","destinationId":"12:3","navigation":"NAVIGATE","transition":null}]},
    {"actions":[{"type":"BACK"}]}]}]}]

What Figma enforces:
- A NAVIGATE to the frame that contains the clicked layer is refused [C-058]: navigate between top-level frames, or use SCROLL_TO or an overlay inside one.
- Smart animate pairs layers across the two frames by name and by place in the hierarchy [C-119]: give every moving layer the same name and nesting in both. A layer only in the destination dissolves in.
- Overlay position, background and click-outside behaviour are read-only to plugins [C-117]: figma_get_reactions reports them; ask the user to set them in Figma's prototype panel.

## Scrolling and fixed layers — figma_set_scroll_behavior
{ nodeId, overflow: "vertical", fixedNodeIds: [<nav id>] }: the frame scrolls in presentation and the nav stays put. Fixed layers are a section at the top of the layer list, not a per-layer flag [C-117], so they are moved there; inside auto-layout make each absolute first (figma_move_nodes { nodeIds, positioning: "absolute" }). A top-level frame larger than the device scrolls on its own; overflow matters for nested frames such as carousels and panels.

## Flows — figma_set_prototype_flows
{ flows: [{ nodeId: <first screen>, name: "Onboarding" }], background: "#111111" } replaces the page's starting points in order; the first is the one the play button opens. Each must be a top-level frame on that page. The call replaces the list, so read the existing flows first (figma_get_reactions { scope: "page" }) and keep the user's own.

Check what you wired with figma_get_reactions; a refusal comes back with Figma's message naming the id or field.
motion:
# Motion — keyframe animation on the timeline

Motion is animation along a frame's timeline (Figma's Motion beta). It is not a prototype transition between frames (topic "prototype"). Figma enables it per user [C-115]: when a motion tool answers UNSUPPORTED, stop — tell the user and deliver the static design; do not retry, and do not fake it with prototype transitions.

## Rules
- Animate the layers INSIDE a top-level frame, never the top-level frame itself: the frame owns the timeline its children play on.
- Manual keyframes (figma_set_keyframes) are the default. Animation styles show in figma_get_motion_context but cannot be applied through figma-mcp yet.
- Times are seconds. Values are strings by field: a number "0.5" (OPACITY, ROTATION, TRANSLATION_X …), a vector "10,20" (TRANSLATION_XY, SCALE_XY), a colour "#ff000080" ("fill:<i>", "stroke:<i>", an effect's COLOR). Only a SOLID paint animates.
- Easing names are Figma's: EASE_IN_AND_OUT, not EASE_IN_OUT. Also LINEAR, EASE_IN, EASE_OUT, the _BACK forms, GENTLE, QUICK, BOUNCY, SLOW, HOLD (a jump), "cubic:x1,y1,x2,y2" and "spring:<bounce 0-1>". A keyframe's easing shapes the move from the previous keyframe into it.
- TRANSLATION and ROTATION add to the resting transform (0 = unchanged; positive ROTATION turns counter-clockwise); SCALE multiplies it (1 = unchanged). OPACITY and the other fields replace the value.
- WIDTH and HEIGHT do not animate on a group or a vector: use SCALE_X / SCALE_Y.
- The timeline grows to fit your last keyframe and is never shortened for you, because other layers share it. Shorten it only on purpose, with `timelineDuration`.

## Recipe — a card that fades and rises in
1. figma_get_motion_context { nodeId: <frame> }: what already moves inside it, and how long the timeline is.
2. figma_set_keyframes { nodeId: <card>, tracks: [
     {"field":"OPACITY","keyframes":[{"t":0,"value":"0"},{"t":0.4,"value":"1","easing":"EASE_OUT"}]},
     {"field":"TRANSLATION_Y","keyframes":[{"t":0,"value":"24"},{"t":0.4,"value":"0","easing":"spring:0.2"}]}] }
3. Stagger siblings: start each one's keyframes a little later (0.06–0.1 s).
4. Verify: figma_export_video { nodeId: <frame>, format: "GIF", fps: 12, width: 480, frames: [0, 0.2, 0.4] }. figma_export_node shows only the resting state [C-116], so judge motion from these frames — one per phase (start, middle, settle), rendered small; fix every problem you see before rendering again.
5. Take a track back with figma_remove_keyframes { nodeId, fields: ["OPACITY"] }.
rules:
# Design-system rules for a codebase

Write a rules section once, so every later design-to-code run in this project makes the same choices. The create_design_system_rules prompt starts this playbook.

1. Read the Figma side:
   - figma_get_variable_defs: every token, with values per mode and codeSyntax.
   - figma_get_styles: text, paint, effect and grid styles with values.
   - figma_get_local_components: components and variant sets (figma_get_component for one's properties).
   - figma_get_design_context on one representative screen: the styles, variables and components (library ones included) a real screen uses.
2. Read the codebase: where components live and how they are named, the token sources (CSS variables, the Tailwind theme, theme objects), the styling approach, and how icons and images are stored.
3. Write ONE section into the client's rules file — AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursor/rules/, or the path the user named. Append; never overwrite what is there. It states:
   - The flow: figma_get_design_context → figma_export_node (the visual target, never an asset) → figma_download_assets { nodeIds, dir: <the project's asset folder> } → implement → render and compare. `dir` must sit inside the export directory or a BRIDGE_EXPORT_ROOTS entry, so the rule also says the asset folder must be listed in BRIDGE_EXPORT_ROOTS; without `dir` the files land in the export directory.
   - Layout: which layout primitives auto-layout maps to.
   - Components: their folder and naming, and a table "Figma component → code component" for those that exist.
   - Tokens: a table "Figma variable or style → code token" (codeSyntax where set), and what must never be hardcoded: colours, spacing, radii, type.
   - Assets: where downloaded images and icons go, and that no icon package is added.
4. Show the user the section and the file it went into.
code-to-design:
# From code to a Figma design

Building in Figma what already exists in code: the code is the brief. Unlike a free brief, do not invent content and do not choose fonts by mood — take both from the source.

1. Read the source the user named and list its sections, the components it renders, and their DEFAULT props. Build the default state first.
2. Font: take the family from the code (CSS variables, Tailwind theme.fontFamily, the theme) and resolve exact Figma family and style names with figma_get_fonts { scope: "available" }. Use Inter only when the code names no font. After building, figma_check_layout { nodeId, audit: ["fonts"], expectFonts: ["<family>"] }: a wrong_font finding, or `fellBack` in a create result, is a failure to fix.
3. Components, in this order:
   - A Code Connect mapping or a Figma link for THIS file names the component: pass its node id as componentId as is.
   - Reuse what existing screens use: figma_get_design_context shows each instance's component id and key; figma_get_local_components lists the rest.
   - Only then build: one main component per source component (props become component properties and variants), then place instances — never several near-identical frames.
4. Icons: the codebase's own SVG through figma_import_svg { svg, width, height, color } (or colorVariable). currentColor imports as black, so pass the colour. Never redraw an icon from lines, rectangles or ellipses.
5. Images: figma_import_image { url }, or { path } for a local file. The bridge reads only inside the export directory or a BRIDGE_EXPORT_ROOTS entry (a relative path resolves from the export directory), so a repository file is refused unless the repository is a root: ask the user to add it to BRIDGE_EXPORT_ROOTS, or copy the file into the export directory first.
6. Tokens: bind the file's variables and styles by name (spec `variables` and `style`). When a value in code and the Figma token disagree, ASK the user which one wins — the one question you do not decide alone.
7. A web app you can open: screenshot it with your browser tool, save it under an export root, place it beside the build with figma_import_image { path } as a reference, compare with figma_export_node, then delete the reference by its returned id.
8. Check as in every build: figma_check_layout per section and one render, then compare with the source once more.
figjam:
# FigJam boards — a wrapper, zones, and connectors last

A board (a figma.com/board/ link) has one page: organise it with sections, not pages. Your work runs through the same loop as a design — plan, build one zone per call, check each zone — with FigJam's own node types.

Board writes are verified live one tool at a time: figma_status lists what this board refuses (`unavailableTools`). A refusal is UNSUPPORTED with safeToRetry true: nothing changed, so use another tool or pass `session` for a file where it runs — do not retry the same call.

## 1. Orient
- figma_status: the session's editor is FigJam. With a Design file connected too, pass `session` on every call.
- figma_get_design_context { absolute: true } reads every board type: stickies, shapes with text, connectors (`from` / `to` in the form the connector tools take, plus a `connectors` edge list), tables, code blocks, sections; `abs` is each node's box on the page. figma_get_metadata adds `board`: the top-level sections and counts by type.
- To find content: figma_search_nodes { text } and figma_scan_text_nodes also search sticky, shape, connector-label and table-cell text.

## 2. Plan the board
- What is it for, who uses it, once or recurring? Match an archetype: retro (lanes), brainstorm (instructions plus zones people fill), decision (context | options | decision), review (a story left to right), flow (a diagram).
- Reading order is left to right, top to bottom: context first, evidence in the middle, the ask last; appendix below.
- Distance carries meaning: items of one thought 60–90 px apart, different topics 200–400, different parts of the board 1000 or more.
- Every board opens with a title at its top-left that reads at overview zoom; a template also gets a short "how to use" zone.

## 3. Structure
- One white wrapper section holds the whole board, so it moves as one unit. Zones are sections inside it; cards are sections inside zones. Frames only for small auto-layout pieces (a badge, a pill).
- A section whose title is a text inside it gets name "" (the label would repeat the title). Keep the name when there is no title text.
- Size from the content outward. A zone people will fill (votes, ideas, feedback) is sized for the expected activity, not for today's content, and gets a few example stickies to show what goes there.
- Spacing on a 4 px grid: zone padding about 68 top, 60 right, 100 bottom, 80 left; 60–64 between items; about 92 between sibling sections and 120 between rows of sections.

## 4. Which node for what
| Need | Node |
|---|---|
| One idea to discuss, vote on or move | sticky |
| Headings, narrative, instructions | text — never stickies |
| A flowchart step, decision, database | shape with text |
| A relation between two nodes | connector |
| Rows and columns of data | table — never a grid of shapes |
| Code | code block |
| A web page | link preview (figma_create_link_preview) |
| A zone or a card | section |
| A numbered marker | shape "label" |

## 5. Type and colour
- Inter throughout. Board title 64–96 Bold, zone heading about 48 Bold, card title 28–32 Semi Bold, body 20–24 Regular (never below 20), metadata 16.
- Text is Charcoal #1E1E1E — the default here. Hierarchy comes from size, never from grey text.
- Colour by NAME, resolved per node type: a blue sticky, a blue connector and a blue shape are three different swatches, and a name lands on FigJam's exact swatch while a hex one channel off shows as a custom colour. Sections take a hex for now; light tints work (#F5FBFF, #EBFFEE, #FFF7F0, #F8F5FF) with white cards inside.
- Gold draws the eye; red means broken, never just "look here"; green only for small status marks.
- Sticky colours can carry meaning: blue discussion, yellow question, green positive, pink concern, red blocker, teal decision, violet idea.

## 6. Build: one zone per call
- First the wrapper: figma_create_from_spec { spec } with a white section (name "", a rough size); every zone then goes into it by parentId.
- Then each zone: figma_create_from_spec { parentId: <wrapper>, spec } — the section, its title, its stickies or cards (`arrange` lays them out from their real sizes, `hug` fits the section), and its connectors by `ref`. Topic "spec" has the fields and a worked retro zone.
- Stickies are 240×240, or 416×240 with `wide` (about 100 words or more); they grow taller with their text and never take a size.
- More stickies into an existing zone: figma_create_stickies { stickies, parentId, columns } — laid out from their real heights with a 64 px gap; `parentOverflow` says when they run past the zone.
- Connectors come LAST, made in their final parent, and are never moved or reparented afterwards: a moved connector keeps a stale route. In a spec they are built after everything else; with figma_create_connectors, after the nodes they join exist. Re-point or restyle one with figma_edit_connectors.
- Board copy: short phrases, no em dashes. A bulleted list is one text with `list`.

## 7. Check every zone
- figma_check_layout { nodeId: <zone>, audit: ["board"] }: section_overflow, sticky_overlap, dangling_connector, label_too_long, text_not_charcoal, off_palette, section_name_duplicate — fix every warning.
- figma_export_node { nodeId: <zone> } once, to judge it.
- figma_fit_sections { nodeIds: [<cards>, <zone>] } on zones holding finished content, inner sections in the same call (fitted first); then the wrapper with padding "68,60,100,80". Never fit a zone sized for people to fill, or one of a row of equal cards.

## 8. Diagrams
The official Figma MCP's generate_diagram is a hosted service: it turns Mermaid or a description into a laid-out diagram. figma-mcp has no such layout engine yet; build diagrams from primitives — shapes with text, joined by connectors by `ref` — in figma_create_from_spec, one zone per call. Keep a call to about 15–20 nodes and split a bigger diagram into zones. Lay rows out with `arrange` ("row", "grid:N"); connectors are elbowed by default; a label is a few words.

## 9. What a board refuses
- Local styles, components and variants (build them in a Design file), keyframe motion and video export: UNSUPPORTED.
- The Slides tools.
- A new page, images and every other write not yet verified on a board — figma_status `unavailableTools` lists them.

## Anti-patterns
- Stickies for narrative text; shapes as decoration; more than one or two emphasis marks per zone.
- Stickies staggered, overlapping or touching a section's edge; one text per bullet.
- The whole board in one call; no wrapper; no title; section labels left on above their own title.
- Body text below 20 px; grey text for hierarchy; red for attention.

# Figma Slides decks — plan, then build in batches of slides

A deck (a figma.com/slides/ link) is a grid: rows (its sections) of 1920×1080 slides. A slide is a frame you build into; the grid and its rows are opaque.

Deck writes are verified live one tool at a time: figma_status lists what this deck refuses (`unavailableTools`). A refusal is UNSUPPORTED with safeToRetry true: nothing changed, so use another tool — do not retry the same call.

## Pick the gear first
- An edit (a word, a colour, a number): make it and match what is there.
- Adding to, improving or restyling a deck: read it first (figma_get_slide_grid, figma_export_node on two or three slides) and match its palette, type and habits. Restyle in place: never delete slides to rebuild them unless the user asks to start over.
- A new deck: design it fully, below.

## Orient
- figma_status: the session's editor is Figma Slides.
- figma_get_slide_grid — rows of slides with ids, names, skipped, notes, title and background. An empty deck has no rows: the first figma_create_slides makes row 0.
- figma_get_design_context { nodeId: <slide id> } for a slide's layers. With nothing selected it reads the focused slide, else the deck's outline.

## A new deck of 5 or more slides
Plan first, without a tool call:
- Read the brief: what the deck must land, and for whom. A brand, a palette or a reference file the user gave you are decisions already made; you decide only what they leave open.
- Per slide: its job, its layout in words ("title upper-left, chart over the right two thirds, a circle bleeding off the top-right"), its background.
- The palette as roles (primary, accent, dark background, surface, text, muted), the fonts, and one signature motif.
- Read the layouts in order: if they repeat, vary them now — this is the cheapest moment.

Then build, 3–5 slides per batch, without re-planning between batches unless one fails:
1. figma_create_slides { slides: [{ "name": "Title", "background": "#0B1020" }, …] } — the batch's empty slides, in order.
2. One figma_create_from_spec { parentId: <slide id>, spec } per slide: `spec` is a JSON array of the slide's roots (title, body, shapes, images), placed with x/y.
3. figma_check_layout { nodeIds: [<the batch's slide ids>] }: out_of_slide, text_cut_by_slide, overlap, low_contrast; bleed is info (deliberate when a shape runs off the edge). Fix before the next batch.
4. figma_export_node on one or two slides after the FIRST batch (does the look work?) and after the LAST (the whole deck) — not after every batch.

An example slide's content, as `spec`:
  [{"type":"rectangle","name":"Accent field","width":760,"height":1080,"x":1160,"y":0,"fill":"#F2C14E"},{"type":"text","name":"Title","content":"Pairing halved our review time","fontSize":96,"weight":"Bold","color":"#0B1020","width":980,"x":120,"y":160},{"type":"text","name":"Points","content":"Two people on every hard bug\nReviews done within a day\nFewer late surprises","list":"unordered","fontSize":36,"color":"#0B1020","width":900,"x":120,"y":560}]

## Rules a deck enforces
- A slide is 1920×1080 and is never resized; a slide is not an auto-layout parent, so its direct children use x/y, not "fill" sizing.
- A background goes on the slide (`background` in figma_create_slides, or figma_set_fills on the slide): rows and the grid take no paint and are never read.
- Each node goes into its parent before its x/y is set; the create result's `drift` lists any position Figma moved. Expect []; never add an offset back by hand.
- Bullets are ONE text with `list` ("unordered" or "ordered") and lines separated by \n — never a dot shape beside each line.
- Reorder with figma_move_slides (a few slides) or figma_set_slide_grid (the whole deck's grouping); copy a slide with figma_clone_node (it lands right after its source); skip one with figma_set_slide_properties.
- Show the user: figma_zoom_to { nodeId: <slide id> } focuses that slide; `view` "grid" or "single-slide".
- The whole deck as one PDF: figma_export_frames_to_pdf { deck: true, outputPath: "deck.pdf" } (skipped slides left out unless includeSkipped).

## Sections
Every row is a section, named in the editor and in Presenter View. Asked to organise a deck, read it and propose a grouping from its own cues (the title, numbered parts, transition slides, a closing) in one message; ask only when it has none. Two to five sections, each named in one to three concrete words; rename a section with figma_rename_node on its row id (figma_get_slide_grid lists them).

## Speaker notes
Only when asked, or for a deck meant to be presented: figma_set_slide_properties { slides: [{ "slideId": "…", "speakerNotes": "- …" }] }. Short markdown bullets that add what the slide does not say — why, the transition to the next slide, a source, the question to expect — never the slide's text again and never a script unless asked. Lists, bold, italic and strikethrough show; headings, code and links stay literal. If this Figma build does not expose notes, the call is refused and nothing changes.

## Design principles
- One colour leads, a second supports, an accent punctuates — chosen for this subject. Dark bookends (title, close) around a lighter middle work well; body text on dark stays near white.
- Hierarchy visible from across the room: the title far larger than the body. Body text is left-aligned; centre only titles and one-line statements. Pair a display face with a workhorse (figma_suggest_fonts).
- One idea per slide. Cut before you shrink: more slides, not denser ones.
- Layout follows what the slide does. Uneven splits (70/30) beat 50/50; vary where content anchors from slide to slide; use the edges, and let a shape bleed off.
- At least one non-text element on every slide, and one recurring motif bold enough to register.
- Avoid: the same layout on every slide, a rule under every heading, every block in a tinted rounded box, faint decoration, flat hierarchy, dense tables.

## Out of reach
- Templates and themes; creating interactive elements (polls, embeds — they are read and can be moved, never created); presenting.
- Transitions: figma_set_slide_transition is unverified, and is refused with nothing changed where this Figma build does not implement them.
- Local styles in a deck are refused; components and variables are unverified writes.
